restoration_note: This teaching describes the four weepings of the rational's outer truths (the 'garments of the sons of the First Man'): three weepings during descent into the contest with the self, and a fourth at the consummation when the Last Andrias ascends and souls who have given themselves to darkness are cut off from the unity. Most gaps were small letter-completions or formulaic continuations strongly constrained by parallel formulas within the chapter itself: ⲥⲱⲭⲡ̄ ⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'remain behind' (§3699/§3700), ⲱⲁⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'cut off from' (§3699/§3709), and the twice-repeated Andrias-ascent formula 'ⲡⲥⲁⲡ ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ ⲉⲧⲉⲣⲉ ⲡⲁⲛⲇⲣⲉⲓⲁⲥ ⲛⲁⲃⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈' (gaps 4–5 mirrored at gaps 20–21). The chapter's leitmotifs of weeping (ⲣⲓⲙⲉ), being cut off (ⲱⲁⲧ), and remaining behind (ⲥⲱⲭⲡ̄) made most gaps confidently fillable. Gaps 25 and 26 — a coupled pair specifying a category alongside 'souls' before whom the firmaments stand concealed — lacked sufficient anchor in surrounding text and were marked unrestorable. Gap 24 (ⲛⲍⲏⲡ 'hidden') was supported by the immediate qualifier 'which stands concealed' but rated moderate due to character-count tension.
